Looking at this problem, I need to analyze the `HelperA.dfy` file and fix the `Prove` lemma body.

The issue is in the `forall` block. When proving that `left[q] == right[q]`, I need to properly handle the cases based on whether `q` is in `n` (not `m`), since `Override(m,n)` gives priority to `n` over `m`.

Let me trace through the logic:
- `merged = Override(m,n)` - keys from both, values from `n` take priority
- `left = Restrict(merged, keep)` - only keys in `keep`
- `rm = Restrict(m, keep)`, `rn = Restrict(n, keep)`
- `right = Override(rm, rn)` - keys from both restrictions, values from `rn` take priority

For any `q in left`:
- `q in merged` and `q in keep`
- `merged[q]` is `n[q]` if `q in n`, else `m[q]`
- `right[q]` is `rn[q]` if `q in rn`, else `rm[q]`
- Since `rn = Restrict(n, keep)`, `q in rn` iff `q in n && q in keep`
- Since `rm = Restrict(m, keep)`, `q in rm` iff `q in m && q in keep`

The key insight is that the condition should be based on `q in n`, not `q in m`. When `q in n`, we need to call `RestrictAt(n, keep, q)` to establish that `rn[q] == n[q]`. When `q not in n`, then `q` must be in `m` (since it's in `merged`), and we call `RestrictAt(m, keep, q)`.

```json
{
  "HelperA.dfy": "var merged := K.Override(m,n);\n    var left := K.Restrict(merged,keep);\n    var rm := K.Restrict(m,keep);\n    var rn := K.Restrict(n,keep);\n    var right := K.Override(rm,rn);\n    D.OverrideKeys(m,n);\n    D.RestrictKeys(merged,keep);\n    D.RestrictKeys(m,keep);\n    D.RestrictKeys(n,keep);\n    D.OverrideKeys(rm,rn);\n    assert left.Keys == right.Keys;\n    forall q | q in left ensures q in right && left[q] == right[q] {\n      V.RestrictAt(merged,keep,q);\n      V.OverrideAt(m,n,q);\n      if q in n {\n        V.RestrictAt(n,keep,q);\n      } else {\n        V.RestrictAt(m,keep,q);\n      }\n      V.OverrideAt(rm,rn,q);\n    }\n    A.Equal(left,right);"
}
```
